channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Stronger fix guides gradual RMB gains – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that USD/CNH dipped after a stronger USD/CNY fix below 6.80, the first such level since February 2023. They read this as policymakers being comfortable with further RMB appreciation while managing the pace.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG downtrend accelerates, eyes on $55.00
item.description: Silver price remains below $60.00 as the week begins, diving nearly 4% on Monday amid tensions in the Middle East. Hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller underpin the Greenback, which, according to the US Dollar Index (DXY), is up by over 0.28%.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as Hormuz tensions and policy concerns weigh
item.description: USD/JPY trades higher near 162.40 on Monday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) weakens amid escalating tensions between the United States (US) and Iran. The US Dollar (USD) remains supported by higher Oil prices and growing concerns that renewed energy pressure could keep global inflation elevated.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rises as Waller puts July Fed rate hike in play, CPI awaited
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) regains momentum on Monday after hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller boosted expectations of an interest rate hike as early as this month.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downside bias within established range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD opened stronger after a quiet prior session, with upward momentum tentatively building but still facing resistance around 1.2945–1.2955. For the next 1–3 weeks, they keep its view that USD/SGD will trade between 1.2890 and 1.2990.

item.title: Gold price crashes as Waller warning sparks Fed hike fears
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) plunges on Monday after remarks by Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller, who revealed that if the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rises this week, the Fed should consider interest rate hikes.

item.title: Crude Oil finds a toll booth where its ceasefire used to be
item.description: Crude Oil is repricing the death of a framework rather than any single missile exchange.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls as US-Iran tensions weigh on risk sentiment
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near 0.6930 on Monday, retreating from an opening level of around 0.6950 as escalating tensions between the United States (US) and Iran bolster the safe-haven US Dollar (USD) and weigh on the risk-sensitive Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: Swiss Franc drops to a more than two-week low against the US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday as traders react to renewed hostilities in the Middle East. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.8126, up 0.50% on the day and marking its highest level since June 25.

item.title: Equities: Positioning signals recovery optionality – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that Emerging Markets (EM) equity positioning is heavily skewed toward South Korea and Taiwan, with the rest of EM seeing historically low allocations. China’s weakness and poor EM data have already driven valuations to price in disinflation and weak growth.

item.title: British Pound falls as Oil shock boosts the US Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling begins the week on a lower note, as over-the-weekend developments in the Middle East fueled inflation expectations due to the rise in Oil prices. At the time of writing, the GBP/USD trades at 1.3369, down over 0.20%.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average wobbles while Washington opens a toll booth in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Risk aversion set Monday's tone, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average wore it better than most of its peers; the index trades near 52,525, down 117 points or 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite sheds 1% and the S&P 500 gives back 0.4%.

item.title: Gold eyes $4,000 as renewed US-Iran hostilities boost Oil prices, Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) starts the week on the back foot as renewed tensions in the Middle East lift Oil prices and bring inflation concerns back into focus, reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike later this year.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains as Oil prices surge on Middle East supply risks
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) outperforms most of its major peers on Monday as renewed tensions in the Middle East push Oil prices higher amid fresh risks of supply disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Commodities: Forward curves and carry framework – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem note that the commodity complex has been resilient to Middle East tensions, with Oil gains capped and forecasts for prices at $70 by year end unchanged.

item.title: President Trump declares US ‘Guardian of the Hormuz Strait’
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump announced that the Strait of Hormuz is open and will remain accessible to international shipping “with or without Iran,” while outlining a new US-led security arrangement for the strategic waterway.

item.title: Denmark: Goods resilience offsets weaker services – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team reports that overall consumer spending excluding energy in June was broadly unchanged on the month, with real spending up 4.3% year-on-year. Real retail spending on goods rose, particularly in larger consumer categories, while service spending generally declined.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Higher energy prices pressure JPY – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the Japanese Yen has weakened again, pushing USD/JPY back above 162.00 as higher energy prices and fading impact from last week’s verbal intervention weigh on the currency.

item.title: US Dollar: CPI, Fed speakers and Warsh testimony – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen highlights a US‑centric data and policy calendar, with June CPI expected to ease to 3.8% year‑on‑year and core inflation to 2.8%.

item.title: Fed: Inflation risks and policy hold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir highlight that the June FOMC minutes were hawkish, with most participants ready to hike if supply-driven inflation persists.

item.title: Switzerland: Federalism and direct democracy as growth drivers – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Jörg Krämer describes Switzerland’s strong federalism and extensive use of financial referenda as key to its superior economic outcomes. Cantons and municipalities compete for taxpayers by setting their own tax rates and controlling spending.

item.title: Why the Swiss Franc isn’t likely to move far from 0.9200 against the Euro
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) trades in a tight range against the Euro (EUR) as the Swiss National Bank (SNB) actively works to neutralize safe-haven capital inflows stemming from increased geopolitical woes.

item.title: Iran warns US against Hormuz transit
item.description: Iran’s top joint military command issued a series of warnings on Monday over the Strait of Hormuz, saying any unauthorized United States (US) transit would be confronted and cautioning neighboring countries against supporting Washington.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains range-bound with a bearish bias
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) attracts sellers on Monday after renewed fighting between the United States (US) and Iran over the weekend revived energy-driven inflation concerns and reinforced expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike later this year.

item.title: Japanese Yen: GPIF narrative keeps FX volatility elevated – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that Japan remains a key source of two‑way FX volatility as markets digest conflicting signals on Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) allocations.

item.title: US Dollar: Geopolitics and inflation risks support Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar (USD) has gained modestly as renewed US–Iran tensions lift Brent Oil back to USD80, with markets rebuilding a geopolitical risk premium.

item.title: Swiss Franc: SNB intervention and cautious policy stance – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley describes how the Swiss National Bank has actively countered safe haven inflows into the Swiss Franc since the Iran war, selling CHF and signalling increased willingness to intervene.

item.title: Oil: Strait of Hormuz risks reshape macro mix – BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu notes that renewed U.S.-Iran tensions have lifted Brent and WTI, with markets reassessing energy supply risks and broader risk sentiment.

item.title: Euro climbs above 1.1400 as US Dollar loses ground
item.description: EUR/USD trades with a mild positive bias on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) gives back its earlier gains. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1424 after recovering from an intraday low of 1.1384.

item.title: US President Trump: We are taking over the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: In an interview with Fox News on Monday, United States (US) President Donald Trump said that they will probably take over the Strait of Hormuz and argued that they should be reimbursed for controlling it.
